trails.title: Training
trails.subtitle: from AII to a Thread node
trails.say: From an app's records in AII to a Thread node: the records become the Thread's corpus, the corpus trains a head in front of the commons' trunk, and the head and its index load as a node.

entries.note: Making a Thread, start to end: the source read into a snapshot, a head trained, the snapshot indexed, the version made live and attached. braid thread create, the studio and the playground all run it.

entries.anchor: public static func read(_ spec: CorpusSourceSpec
entries.note: Every source a Thread can start from meets here: a dataset node, a folder, Braid's own AII lane, or an app's records. Each comes back as the same snapshot, so nothing after this point knows where the text came from.
An app's records are read from the app's own lane, under the owner that lane names. Braid reads exactly what that app filed and nothing beside it.
Exports every record under the app's id prefix, 25 to a page, because each record carries its envelope. The snapshot remembers the lane, so verify can re-read a citation from the same place later.

entries.anchor: guard page.hasMore_p, let last = page.documents.last else { break }
entries.note: Pages through AII's export until it says there is no more, with each page's last id as the cursor. Search would return what looks relevant; training needs every word, so Braid exports.
The request itself: an owner, its groups, an id prefix and a cursor. It asks for embeddings because only then does the Thread service describe each partition with its id and URL.
Every source ends as this snapshot, sorted by document id. Its corpus hash is the receipt for exactly what a Thread learned from.
The SHA-256 of one line per partition: document, partition, and the hash of its text. It sorts first, so the hash depends on what the corpus holds and never on the order it arrived in.
A new Thread is a folder holding its record and the snapshot filed under its corpus hash. Nothing is trained yet.

steps.title: The same words, and the commons

entries.note: Text becomes token ids in the commons' own GPT-NeoX vocabulary, with no special tokens added. Every strand must share this vocabulary before it may join a braid.
Each document becomes eos, its partitions joined by the paragraph break, and eos again, and every token remembers its row and offset. Those two numbers are the address a citation points at.
Loading a pack re-hashes every array against its record and refuses any difference. A Thread trained against one trunk must never meet another.

entries.anchor: let node = try ThreadStore.commons(pack: pack, scheme: defaultKey(packRecord))
entries.note: Before any head is made, the engine builds the commons, once. Every head it trains or indexes runs in front of that one trunk.

entries.anchor: trunk: try Trunk(pack: pack), index: nil
entries.note: The commons as a node: the pack's trunk whole, no index, λ 0. Here it lends its trunk; in a braid it is also the yardstick.
The commons: the pack run whole, every block frozen, and the seam re-derived from what it holds. Its blocks 12 to 23, its embedding and its final norm are the trunk every Thread runs.
The reed is the embedding itself, transposed: tied, as the commons was trained. Training scores the head through it, and the braid reads every strand through the same one.

steps.title: A head on the commons' trunk

entries.anchor: let trunk = Trunk(head: head, tail: try commons().trunk.tail)
entries.note: The trunk a Thread trains on: a head in front of the commons' tail. A new Thread's head starts as the pack's own first twelve blocks, and a sync's as the live version's.
The pack's own blocks 0 to 11, as imported and ready to train. Every Thread's head starts as these twelve.
A head is blocks 0 to 11 and nothing else: a file that holds a block of the trunk is refused, and so is one that lacks a block of its own. A version keeps the head on disk and nothing more.
A Thread's running model: its head in front of the commons' tail. The twelve shared blocks are not copied; the Thread holds the commons' own instances.
The training stage: the snapshot as tokens, and the head trained in place on them. Only the head's blocks change; the commons' trunk is the same object before and after.

Trains a Thread's own blocks in place: windows from the stream, AdamW, a clipped gradient, and an evaluation every few epochs that stops once the corpus is learned. Backprop runs through all 24 blocks, but only the twelve below the cut move.
The whole corpus becomes one stream with eos between documents. A transformer would need a document mask here; a Mamba state is simply reset at every eos.
Each epoch cuts the stream into windows on a grid shifted by a seeded offset, then shuffles them. The same seed gives the same plan, so a run can be repeated exactly.
A short warmup, then a cosine from the peak rate down to the final one.

Builds inputs, targets, a mask and resets for each window. Wherever the input is eos the loss is masked and the state is reset, so every document is learned as if it were read alone, the way the index reads it.
The loss: a forward pass with resets, the reed, and cross-entropy over the unmasked tokens. It runs under valueAndGrad, which is why Braid wrote its own scan.
Scores every document from a zero state. A token is memorised when its loss is under 0.1 nat, and a version is learned when 97% of the corpus and 90% of its facts are.
The index stage reads the snapshot again, through the freshly trained head and the commons' trunk, and keys it into a new version's folder.
A new version's folder: the head saved as blocks.safetensors, its twelve blocks and nothing of the trunk, then the index built beside it.
Reads every document whole from a zero state, one segment at a time, and joins what each adds into the index.
Records at each position its key, the next token, both addresses and the loss. It saves the state at partition boundaries once 1,024 tokens have passed, so any key can be recomputed later.
The key is the normalised middle state and the normalised final state, side by side, half and half: 1,536 numbers. The raw state would be 789,504 bytes a position, so it is not the key.
The version's record is written, then the version goes live. A new Thread says so, with its entries and how much of its corpus it memorised.
A version records every hash it rests on: pack, seam, vocabulary, tokenizer, blocks, index, checkpoints and corpus. A node that loads it can prove what it is.
Making a version live is one small file that names it.
The last stage puts the Thread on braid.toml's attach list, so the studio and braid chat load it from then on.

entries.anchor: let trunk = Trunk(head: head, tail: tail)
entries.note: Where training ends: the live version as a node. Its head comes from blocks.safetensors and runs in front of the commons' tail, its index loads beside it, and every hash is checked on the way.
The version's seam and cut, then the index's, against the tail the head is about to run on. One trunk per Thread, for its whole life.
The node itself: one trunk, its index, and a descriptor that names every hash a braid checks before it lets the node in. The commons is the same kind of node, with no index.

trails.title: Inference
trails.subtitle: from a prompt to its receipt
trails.say: From a prompt to a checked answer: the braid assembles, every strand reads the prompt and steps word by word, and each word is weighed, chosen, logged and checked.

entries.note: A braid starts with the commons: the pack whole, no index, λ 0. It comes first because every Thread runs behind its trunk.

entries.anchor: try checkSeam(version, index: index.info, tail: tail, thread: name)
entries.note: A Thread is loaded behind the commons and names the seam it was trained against. Before its head runs on the commons' trunk, the two seams must agree, or the Thread is refused.
A node joins the braid now, or at the next word boundary when an answer is already being written.

entries.anchor: let steps = try node.open(session: sessionID, tokens: tokens, k: settings.k)
entries.note: Admission: the node's descriptor is checked against the braid, its partitions take the next rows of the braid's table, and a node that joins mid-answer reads the words so far in one pass to catch up.

entries.anchor: throw Failure.seam(node: descriptor.name, expected: seamSHA256, found: found)
entries.note: A node joins only if it can share the reed: the braid's vocabulary, width and tokenizer, its pack, and its seam. A Thread trained against another trunk is turned away here.
One generation: the prompt is read and moves the gate, then each new word is guessed, weighed, chosen and logged, and every node advances. Strands attach and detach between words.
A session starts with one forward pass over the prompt from a zero state, returning every position's state and its sixteen hits. A node that attaches mid-answer catches up the same way.
The starting point: a zero state for each of the 24 layers. A document is read from here in training, in the index and in a session.
One pass over many tokens: the embedding, the head's twelve blocks, the commons' twelve, the final norm. It can tap the residual after any block, which is where the key's middle half comes from.
The chunked scan, in plain MLX operations with no eval inside, so it can run under a gradient. Resets split it into segments, so packed documents come out exactly as if each ran alone.
One token in: one step of the trunk, one key, one search. The node sends back its normed state and its hits and nothing else, so every number after this can be recomputed from the log.

One token through the same 24 blocks, the Thread's own and then the commons', carrying the state forward. Every strand advances this way while it answers: no cache that grows, one state of fixed size.
A block is x plus its mixer over the normed x, exactly as imported. Mamba2 has no MLP blocks, and adding one would break the import.
The mixer for one token: a projection, a causal convolution over a short window, the selective state update, a gated norm, and out. Its memory is the convolution window and the state.
The recurrence itself: the old state decays and the new input is written in. Everything that came before lives in this state, which is why it can stand where attention keeps its cache.
The size of a strand's whole history: every layer's state and convolution window in f32, 19,390,464 bytes at 130m. It does not grow with the text.
The key's middle half. Under the default scheme, residual:12, it is the residual stream after block 12, just past a Thread's own blocks. The sweep tried ten schemes and this one won.
At every word the node keys its own state exactly as the index keyed its corpus. A key close to one in the index means a place in the text that reads like this moment.
The commons has no index, so it returns no hits. A Thread searches its own.

Search is one matrix multiply against every key in the corpus, a partial sort to the best 24, and an exact sort to the top sixteen. Ties go to the earlier entry, so the same key always returns the same hits.

entries.anchor: row: valueRow[entry], offset: valueOffset[entry], loss: loss[entry]
entries.note: A hit carries its own address and loss as well as its score and value, so a log can be checked without the index.

steps.title: Guess, evidence, the gate, one word

entries.note: The braid's one reed: each strand's 768 numbers times the transposed embedding, with the padding rows masked away. The cluster runs it, not the node.
Turns one strand's hits and logits into its two distributions: the evidence from its hits, weighted by score, and the guess from the reed.

entries.anchor: let exps = scores.map { exp(($0 - top) / t) }
entries.note: Softmax of the scores over τ, 0.05. The temperature is sharp, so the closest hit takes most of the weight unless others are nearly as close.

entries.anchor: for p in probabilities where p > 0 { h -= p * log(p) }
entries.note: Shannon entropy in nats. The same function gives H_lm from the reed and H_knn from the hits, and those two are the only entropies the log stores.
A strand's own blend for one word: λ of its evidence and the rest from its guess, with λ 0.5 for a Thread and 0 for the commons.
At every prompt word, each Thread's lift over the commons moves its memory, clamped so no single word moves it past ten to one. Generated words add no evidence.
A strand stays in the mixture while its gate is above the floor. The leader and the commons are always in.
The open strands' gates, rescaled to sum to one: the w′ every share is made from.
The braid's distribution over the next word: each open strand's guess and evidence, weighted by w′. It is one sum, so each strand's part of it is exact.

entries.anchor: return ageA != ageB ? ageA < ageB : a < b
entries.note: The likeliest word wins. A near tie goes to the oldest cited document, then the lower token id, so the same numbers always pick the same word.
The β4 trace gate RaoLM settled on, computed beside the live gate and logged as a shadow. It is never applied.

entries.anchor: let shares = Mixer.shares(mixture, experts: expertsAt, token: y)
entries.note: Writes down everything a word needs to be checked later: each strand's memory, w′, probabilities, share, both entropies, its hits, its trace and the shadow gate.
Each strand's share of the chosen word: its w′ times its probability, over the braid's. The shares sum to one.
Follows chains through a Thread's text: a chain grows only when the word written is the word its document holds next. The longest live chain, past 24 tokens, is the trace.
Feeds the trajectory module both entropies and the lift at every position. Its reading is logged, and reaches the gate only through κ, which is 0.
One line of JSON per position. The log is the artifact: the rest of the receipt is derived from it.
Closes a generation with the SHA-256 of its body, so a single edited line is caught.
Derived when the log is read: runs of three or more words whose top hits walk one partition in order become spans, and verify re-reads each from its source.
Form words go to the commons. Content words go to each strand by its share, weighted by how surprising the commons found them, in bits.
Per Thread, the words it led, its summed share and its credit; per document, the words whose heaviest hit points there. A view of the log, never stored.
Reads a log back and recomputes each generation's body hash as it goes.
Replays the arithmetic: the body hash, shares that sum to one, w′ from memory, every probability and share, H_knn from the hits, and the gate's memory word by word, which proves the clamp held.
braid verify in one call: the arithmetic, the trace replayed over each Thread's index layout, and every span re-read from its source.

entries.anchor: state = try StateStack.load(from: url, expecting: trunk.config)
entries.note: With --keys, verify goes one step further: it recomputes each cited key from the nearest saved state, after checking the state file's hash and the token prefix it is bound to. A key can be audited without keeping a cache.

trails.title: Q/A training
trails.subtitle: facts learned, then measured
trails.say: Braid trains nothing on questions. A Thread learns its facts the way it learns the rest of its corpus, word for word: a dataset brings them, training counts them, and the question bench measures how questions reach them.

entries.anchor: return SourceRead(snapshot: made, facts: generated.facts, lane: nil)
entries.note: Only a dataset node brings facts. An app's records and a folder bring none, so their Threads train with no facts to count.
A dataset node's documents become the snapshot. Its facts travel beside the text, never inside it.
A fact: its subject, the sentence it sits in, where its answer starts and ends, the sentence before it, and the questions that ask for it.
A question about the fact, with the stem the corpus would phrase it as. The bench holds the commons' rewrite against this stem.
Before training, the stage places the facts on the corpus's own tokens.

Each fact's byte offsets become token positions in its partition: the answer's first and last token, and where the sentence before it starts. A fact whose answer does not start on a token boundary is set aside.
A fact on the tokens: its row, the first token of its context sentence, and its answer's span.
Training is the same as for any corpus, and no question is ever shown. The facts only decide when it stops.
A fact counts as memorised only when every token of its answer is, each under 0.1 nat.
The bar a version must clear: 97% of the corpus and 90% of its facts, each token under 0.1 nat. With no facts, only the corpus half counts.

steps.title: An index the answers read from

entries.note: The index stores, at every position, the token that comes next. Read in order, those values are the corpus again, and a question's context sentence will come from them.
Loading the index brings back every position's value and its row, so a Thread can find a hit's document and read the sentence before it.

entries.anchor: let adapter = QuestionAdapter(trunk: commonsNode.trunk, reed: braid.reed, tokenizer: tokenizer)
entries.note: braid bench question asks each fact's first question four ways: through the commons' rewrite as chat does, with the stored stem, with the corpus slice before the answer, and as a paraphrase.
Q1 compares the commons' stem with the stored one, word by word.

The rules, fixed before the numbers and read on the commons' arm. On 2026-10-15 Q1 failed at 7% and Q2 at 10% exact, against 30% for the stored stem; Q3 passed, with 14 of 14 exact answers citing the fact's partition.

trails.title: Q/A inference
trails.subtitle: a question to a cited answer
trails.say: A prompt that ends in a question mark takes the question path: the commons rewrites it into a stem, each Thread finds its own context, and the braid completes the stem behind them, stopping at the end of the sentence.

entries.note: A prompt that ends in a question mark is a question. braid chat, braid bench question and the studio with Q/A on all send it down one path.

entries.anchor: if given == nil, let adapter { rewrite = adapter.rewrite(question, maxTokens: rewriteTokens) }
entries.note: The commons rewrites the question, unless a stem is given, and then every Thread looks for its own context.

steps.title: The commons rewrites it into a stem

entries.note: The commons continues the prompt greedily until it writes the blank, at most 24 tokens. It never sees a Thread's facts.
The prompt is ten public question and stem pairs, then the question. The commons is shown examples, never trained.
Keeps what comes before the blank, without a trailing question mark or colon.
A rewrite is refused when it is empty, still a question, starts with a question word, or drops a capitalised word of the question. Then the question itself becomes the stem.

entries.anchor: if let found = try node.context(stem: tokens, subject: subject, k: k, floor: floor) { contexts[name] = found }
entries.note: The stem becomes tokens, its subject is placed, and each Thread is asked for a context.
A leading space, so a Thread's context and the stem join into the tokens of the joined text.
The subject is the question's capitalised words after the first.

entries.anchor: guard let head = joined.range(of: first) else { return nil }
entries.note: Finds the stem's tokens that write the subject, matching words rather than tokens.

steps.title: Each Thread finds its own context

entries.anchor: try context(stem: stem, subject: subject, k: k, floor: floor, maxTokens: 48)
entries.note: Each Thread looks in its own index for the place it has seen this stem's template, in a document about the subject. The commons has no index and answers on the bare stem.

entries.anchor: for hit in hitsByStemPosition[j] where hit.score >= floor
entries.note: The stem is read through the Thread's own trunk and searched at its template positions. A hit counts at a score of 0.6 or more, in a document that names the subject; behind the best one, the context is the sentence before the hit's, read from the index's values.
A sentence ends at a full stop, a question or exclamation mark, or a line break. A paragraph break belongs to the sentence it closes.

entries.anchor: try cluster.generate(prompt: turn.prompt, contexts: turn.contexts, params: parameters(params))
entries.note: The braid completes the stem, each Thread behind its own context.
An answer stops at the end of its sentence.

entries.anchor: guard !member.descriptor.isCommons, let context = contexts[member.descriptor.name] else { return nil }
entries.note: Each Thread's context goes into the log with its document, row and offset. The commons never has one.
Every Thread opens on its own context and then the stem; the commons opens on the bare stem. The context words are logged and run through the trace, and the gate observes none of them.
The stop: the text so far ends in a full stop, a question or exclamation mark, and the next token starts with a space or a capital, or holds a line break.

When several Threads hold the same fact, the trajectory decides. Per sentence, the Thread whose chains advanced on the most tokens, by a margin of two, takes the credit of every token two or more Threads hold; weight never decides.

entries.anchor: if step.source == .ctx, let owner = step.owner, current.indices.contains(owner) {
entries.note: Verify reads each context line as its owner's alone, and replays it with the rest of the answer.
